latest_final: The wordplay is on “courses” and “student.” You were a student at the University of Hong Kong attending a formal dinner in a residential hall. The “courses” were not classes but the dishes of a multi-course meal. Before the dinner you selected your dishes, which is the sense in which you had to “choose courses.” When the dishes were served, you tasted them and disliked the flavor, so you sent each course back as unsatisfactory, and no replacement was provided. Because you rejected every dish, all of your chosen courses were removed by the end of the evening—so “all of my courses were gone in one evening.” The apparent course-enrollment deadline and disappearance of classes are a misleading framing; the real event was a hall dinner at which every dish you had chosen was sent back and cleared away.
